data.title: AI Agents Can Now Buy Computing With Bitcoin—Does Lightning Have Its Use Case?
data.description:
AI agents have a new way to spend Bitcoin: buying the computing needed to keep working. Lightning Labs has launched pi402, a tool that lets coding agents pay for AI inference over the Lightning Network.

The November 12 announcement moves the agent-payments debate toward a specific purchase. Rather than imagining software shopping autonomously for everything, it starts with a recurring need: access to an AI model that can process the next prompt.

“Inference is the fuel every agent runs on,” Lightning Labs’ Olaoluwa Osuntokun wrote. The business question is whether a Bitcoin payment can make that fuel easier to buy and sell.

How AI agents use Bitcoin for inference

Pi402 connects the Pi coding-agent environment with paid inference services. The launch describes an embedded Wavelength wallet and controls for per-request spending and daily budgets. A human still funds the wallet and sets the operating boundaries.

The attraction is access without creating a separate buyer account or supplying a card to each participating seller. That does not make the entire AI service anonymous, unregulated or free of provider conditions. It changes the payment and access mechanism for services that implement it.

According to the L402 documentation, a buyer first requests a protected resource. The server returns a payment-required response, a credential and a Lightning invoice. Paying produces proof that can be presented with the credential to gain access.

The payment becomes part of authorisation rather than an invoice to settle later. The documentation also describes restricting and delegating bearer credentials, which matters when one piece of software needs to give another a limited ability to buy or access resources.

The useful detail is metering, not a payment for every word

The Aperture v0.6.0 release notes describe prepaid bundles that are drawn down according to actual usage. A single Lightning payment can therefore support multiple model requests. The system does not need to initiate a separate payment for every generated token.

The proxy obtains a price, reserves an estimated amount for a request and accounts for the reported usage afterward. When the remaining balance cannot cover another request, it can issue a new payment challenge.

That distinction separates a plausible billing system from a flashy demonstration. Model responses vary in length. Sellers need a way to price that uncertainty, and buyers need to see what they have actually consumed.

The same release supports both L402 and the Payment HTTP Authentication Scheme used by the Machine Payments Protocol. Supporting more than one payment-authentication format could help services meet different clients, although compatibility by itself does not establish commercial adoption.

The seller still has costs, accounts and exchange-rate exposure

Lightning Labs’ public Lightmeter repository shows another important layer. It converts a provider’s dollar-denominated model prices into millisatoshis per token, can add a seller margin and reconciles usage against the provider’s billing records.

A millisatoshi is one-thousandth of a satoshi. That granularity allows small accounting units, but the conversion does not make the underlying computing free or ensure that Bitcoin-denominated prices stay constant.

The repository’s architecture places the upstream provider’s API key at the proxy. In other words, removing an API key from the buyer’s experience does not necessarily remove API keys from the supply chain. Someone still needs to secure the provider relationship and pay its bill.

That gives the story a more grounded commercial angle. A reseller could offer a narrow, paid entry point to computing while managing procurement and billing behind it. Whether that arrangement is attractive depends on price, reliability, model access and the terms of the upstream service.

Why irreversible payments are a trade-off

Osuntokun argues that card chargebacks are poorly matched to computing that has already been consumed. A completed response cannot be ungenerated so that a seller can recover the electricity and GPU time.

Final payment can reduce that particular uncertainty for a seller. For a buyer, however, it raises the importance of spending controls and service quality. Paying successfully establishes access; it does not prove that an answer is correct or that an autonomous workflow was worth its cost.

BNC’s coverage of Claude Fable and Mythos 5.2 examined falling model prices alongside the continuing need for human judgment. Automating payment makes that distinction more consequential: a system can spend efficiently while pursuing an unhelpful task.

The adoption test starts with something measurable

The launch supplies software and an identifiable use case, rather than evidence that a large new market already exists. The announcement does not establish independent transaction volume, recurring demand or a broad network of competing sellers.

Useful follow-up evidence would include repeat purchases, the number of active providers, total payment costs and how often spending limits prevent unwanted work. Those measures would help distinguish a convenient developer tool from a meaningful new source of Lightning usage.

For Bitcoin, the opportunity is straightforward: a machine-native service being bought through a machine-readable payment. Pi402 makes that proposition testable. Its success will depend on whether developers keep choosing it after the novelty of an agent with a wallet has worn off.

data.title: Indonesia seeks to preserve historic railway assets as part of global heritage
data.description:
Semarang, Indonesia, Nov 14, 2026 - (ACN Newswire) - Indonesia's historic railway infrastructure represents an important part of global transportation heritage that must be preserved while adapting to modern development, according to an Indonesian architecture expert.

Ikaputra, a professor of architecture at Gadjah Mada University (UGM), said Java's railway system reflects the evolution of transportation technology and its influence on urban development, economic activity, and social transformation.

Speaking at the "Heritage Reimagined" architecture seminar during Rail Heritage Forum 2026 in Semarang, Central Java, Indonesia on November 9, he emphasized that Indonesia's railway infrastructure should be recognized as both a national historical asset and part of global railway heritage.

Indonesia's railway history dates back to 1867, when construction of the country's first railway line began in Central Java.

According to Ikaputra, railway heritage includes historic stations, tracks, engineering technologies, and operational facilities that have shaped communities for generations.

He stressed that conservation efforts must protect the historical and architectural significance of these assets while allowing them to remain relevant to contemporary society.

Meanwhile, President Director of state railway operator PT Kereta Api Indonesia (KAI) Bobby Rasyidin reaffirmed the company's commitment to preserving its extensive historical assets alongside modernizing railway operations.

"Beyond managing extensive railway assets, KAI also carries a rich historical legacy. That is why we are focused not only on railway operations but also on protecting and preserving our numerous cultural heritage sites," Bobby said.

He noted that railways played an important role in Indonesia's history, including supporting transportation during the country's struggle for independence.

Bobby also revealed plans to revive historic mining railway routes in West Sumatra, connecting Padang Panjang, Singkarak, and Sawahlunto, as part of the company's heritage preservation efforts.

"In West Sumatra, God willing, we will revive the historic mining railway routes, from Padang Panjang and Singkarak to Sawahlunto," he said.

"To shape the future, we must never forget where we came from," Bobby added.

Organized by KAI under the theme "1867 & Beyond: Preserving the Past, Shaping the Future," Rail Heritage Forum 2026 brought together academics, heritage experts, and railway stakeholders to explore ways to safeguard Indonesia's railway history for future generations.

--Antara

Source: PT Kereta Api Indonesia (Persero)

data.title: Boston Fed's Collins Backs Gradual Rate Increases as Inflation Broadens — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Megan Leonhardt

Boston Federal Reserve President Susan Collins is on board with more higher interest rates, but she's a fan of a gradual approach — further piling on to expectations that a December rate increase is a lock and strengthening the case for 2027 hikes.

"I would currently see a steady, gradual approach as potentially being appropriate in this context," Collins said when speaking with reporters on Saturday during the Boston Fed's annual economic conference, which focused on the housing market. "The price data we've seen over the past three months, and the labor market on a stronger footing, does make me think that the path of policy, of rates, over the next year might be a bit higher than I had thought a couple of months ago."

But Collins, who is not currently a voting member of the rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee, said that given the continued geopolitical and economic uncertainty, the exact path will need to be decided meeting by meeting as data becomes available. She said she believes that a "gradual path is the better way to stitch through" the persistent risks.

"I think the direction for monetary policy is clear, I don't want to get out ahead of how quickly it makes sense to move or how much to move rates," Collins said.

Collins defended the Fed's slow approach so far to raising rates. The central bank tightened monetary policy by a quarter of a percentage point to 3.75% to 4.00% in September, but kept rates steady in October. There's ongoing uncertainty that officials must weigh, Collins said. It is plausible, for example, that the rise in medium- and longer-term rates since the beginning of the year may actually weigh on demand more than expected or that enthusiasm around artificial intelligence investment wanes and creates economic shocks, Collins said. In those scenarios, there may be a greater risk to the economy associated with an aggressive rate hiking cycle.

On inflation, Collins said that she's carefully watching the data to see if price pressures related to the recent shocks, for example, in energy, are broadening out. The October consumer price index reading, which was hotter than expected, did show much broader pressures. Prices on everyday things, from groceries to home furnishings to medical services, experienced large increases last month. Even when excluding the effects of the oil shock and volatile food prices, core inflation translated into an annual growth rate of 2.8%, up from September's 2.6% pace.

Tariffs are also still a factor Collins is monitoring. Goods price inflation, for example, had been deflationary, but that component has risen a bit. In September, good inflation was up 0.7% year-over-year.

Inflation has been elevated for a long time, Collins acknowledged, saying that the Fed needs to follow up on its commitment to bring inflation back down to 2%. She said "some further tightening of monetary policy is appropriate."

Looking at employment conditions, Collins said she's less concerned. The "unusual stability" of the labor market has prevailed, she said, adding that it's "on somewhat more solid footing." While there's been less dynamism in the labor market in recent years due to a lower supply of available workers, she sees it largely in balance — and said that there is the potential for more growth than the U.S. has experienced so far over the past two years.

The fact that hiring has broadened across sectors is also giving her some comfort. Up until recently, month job growth was heavily concentrated in healthcare and social assistance, a situation that made labor conditions more vulnerable to shocks.

The recent strength of the labor market — payrolls gained 165,000 and unemployment ticked down to 4.1% in October — may be a sign of things to come. Collins said that she's hearing from employers in her district that companies are looking to hire.

"It's an unusual labor market, in my view. But what I see is stability and, somewhat more strength — with the potential that we could see more tightening," Collins said.

Write to Megan Leonhardt at megan.leonhardt@barrons.com

data.title: Ashok Leyland Q2 results: Profit climbs 8.7% to ₹891 crore, revenue jumps on MHCV growth
data.description:
Commercial vehicles (CV) major Ashok Leyland Ltd reported an 8.7 per cent increase in consolidated net profit at ₹891 crore for the second quarter ended September 2026 as against ₹820 crore in the same quarter last year.

Consolidated revenue from operations rose 35 per cent and stood at ₹17,030 crore in Q2 FY27.

A 45 per cent jump in the cost of materials and services consumed at ₹9,899 crore weighed on the profitability.

On a standalone basis, net profit rose 13 per cent to ₹869 crore. Revenue grew 39 per cent to ₹13,364 crore.

In a statement, the company said that its CV volumes went up 32 per cent to 64,677 units, compared with 49,116 units in the corresponding quarter last year.

data.title: Musk defends Huang, says NVIDIA will have supply chain issues without him
data.description:
Key points:
  • SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said that NVIDIA will suffer from supply chain issues with former CEO Jensen Huang ousted.
  • "Jensen drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia, but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract," the Tesla CEO said in a Saturday morning X post. "Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost."
  • Musk made the comment in response to an Nov. 12 interview SemiAnalysis CEO Dylan Patel had with CNBC's "Squawk Box Asia."
  • "If Jensen gave me his word about compute delivery or I asked for components to be accelerated, he always came through," Musk wrote in a separate Saturday morning post. "Sure, we'd put together a purchase order at some point later, but I never for a second thought it wouldn't happen."
  • On Friday, Musk said there is a petition circulating to have Huang reinstated, and he will sign it.

data.title: Innovative Immunology Biotech Windward Bio Lists on Nasdaq
data.description:
SHANGHAI, Nov. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Windward Bio, a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and a clinical-stage biotechnology company, successfully listed on Nasdaq on November 13, 2026. Windward Bio (Nasdaq: WWB) priced its IPO at $17.00 per share. Its shares closed at $28.50 on the first trading day, up 68% from the IPO price, giving the company a market capitalization of approximately $1.69 billion. This is Qiming Venture Partners' 11th IPO in 2026.

Qiming Venture Partners invested in Windward Bio's inaugural Series A financing in 2025 and continued to support the company in its Series B financing in 2026. Qiming also participated in this IPO financing round.

Windward Bio was founded in 2024 with a mission to transform the treatment paradigm for patients living with chronic inflammatory diseases through the development of differentiated biologic therapies targeting clinically validated disease pathways. Led by a team with extensive expertise across discovery, development, and commercialization, Windward Bio is advancing a pipeline of ultra-long-acting antibody medicines to improve clinical outcomes, reduce treatment burden and expand treatment options for patients with serious respiratory and dermatologic diseases, including asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and atopic dermatitis.

Windward Bio's lead program, WIN378, is a potentially novel anti-TSLP monoclonal antibody engineered for improved potency and extended half-life. WIN378 is currently being evaluated in POLARIS-1, a Phase 2/3 study in severe uncontrolled asthma, and SIRIUS, a Phase 2 study in COPD. The company's pipeline also includes WIN027, a clinical-stage, long-acting bispecific antibody targeting TSLP and IL-13 with potential applications across multiple inflammatory and immunological diseases. Windward Bio holds exclusive global rights (excluding Greater China and certain Asian countries) to WIN378 through a licensing agreement with Kelun-Biotech and Harbour BioMed, and has separately licensed WIN027 from Qyuns Therapeutics.

"Qiming Venture Partners invests in differentiated, globally competitive biotech innovation designed to address significant unmet needs for patients, and Windward Bio exemplifies this approach. We believe novel, long-acting biologics will reshape the treatment of severe chronic respiratory and skin diseases, and that WIN378 and WIN027 have the potential to expand and meaningfully improve the treatment options available to patients. In the hands of Luca and his team, with their expertise and proven track record, Windward is well-positioned to deliver on this potential, and we look forward to supporting the company through its next phase of growth," said Alexander Sinclair Wilson, Principal at Qiming Venture Partners.

About Qiming Venture Partners

Qiming Venture Partners was founded in 2006. Currently, Qiming Venture Partners manages eleven US Dollar funds and seven RMB funds with $9.5 billion in capital raised. Since our establishment, we have invested in outstanding companies in the Technology and Healthcare industries at the early and growth stages.

Since our debut, we have backed over 630 fast-growing and innovative companies. Over 290 of our portfolio companies have achieved exits through IPOs at the NYSE, NASDAQ, HKEX, Shanghai Stock Exchange, or Shenzhen Stock Exchange, or through M&A or other means. There are also over 110 portfolio companies that have achieved unicorn or super unicorn status.

Many of our portfolio companies are today's most influential firms in their respective sectors, including Xiaomi, Meituan, Bilibili, Zhihu, Roborock, Hesai Technology, UBTech, WeRide, HyperStrong, Insta360, Unisound, Biren Technology, Z.AI, Gan & Lee Pharmaceuticals, Tigermed, Zai Lab, CanSino Biologics, Schrödinger, APT Medical, Sanyou Medical, AmoyDx, SinocellTech, Insilico Medicine, AusperBio, Yuanxin Technology, Medilink Therapeutics, LaNova Medicines, StepFun, among many others.

data.title: What's Fueling the Real-Estate Frenzy ?Taking Over Palm Beach This Week — WSJ
data.description:
By E.B. Solomont

A $75 million teardown. A compound trading hands for $84 million. A renovated estate asking $100 million.

Those were just three of this week's real-estate listings and deals in Palm Beach, Fla. On the affluent barrier island, the uber-wealthy have been gobbling up property since Covid and never really stopped. But as a real-estate reporter for The Wall Street Journal, covering three major properties in as many days was a lot, so I set out to find out what's behind the frenzy.

"The Season" has started

The peak social season in Palm Beach typically runs from late fall to early spring, so the uber-wealthy are in town and making real-estate moves. Meanwhile, deals that went into contract months ago are now closing in time for the season. "You have to be looking in August, September, October to enjoy it by November," said Margit Brandt of Premier Estate Properties, who recently represented Netscape co-founder Jim Clark in his purchase of a waterfront compound for $84 million, plus furniture and art, for almost $100 million in total. "The waterfront here is what's really moving," Brandt said.

Art Basel is coming, and so are the billionaires

Local agents said the flurry of big listings is also driven in part by the upcoming Art Basel art fair in December. While it takes place in Miami Beach, Palm Beach agents said there will be an influx of wealth into South Florida for the event around that time.

The midterm elections could be another potential factor behind the recent market activity, according to Carmen D'Angelo Jr. of Premier Estate Properties, who said some high-net worth individuals feel targeted by political rhetoric on the left and see Palm Beach as a safe haven.

Deals above $50 million have normalized

Several top agents said they are having the best years of their career, surpassing the heady days of 2021 and 2022. At least eight homes have sold for $50 million or more so far this year, compared with six last year, according to public records and data analysis by The Wall Street Journal.

Eight- and nine-figure prices are no longer surprising, said Gary Pohrer of Serhant, who is representing the buyer of a $40 million compound set to close in December. "The buyer asked, 'Am I overpaying?'" he said. "I said you're paying more than it's technically worth, but I can't find you another one."

Inventory is nonexistent

The number of single-family homes for sale in Palm Beach is down about 30% compared with last year, said Dana Koch of the Corcoran Group, who said inventory has been "persistently low" since Covid. "We don't have many ready, willing and able sellers."

Land prices are soaring

Scarce inventory is driving up land prices. Developer Todd Michael Glaser and a partner recently went into contract to buy a home on roughly 2 acres for $160 million — though later backed out over fears a neighbor could block development. Koch recently listed a potential teardown on the Intracoastal Waterway for $75 million.

Home prices are up — by a lot

The ultra high-end market is driving the market in Palm Beach. The median sale price was $12 million during the third quarter, up 20% from $9.9 million in the same period of last year. Turnkey properties command a premium, Brandt said. "People want to have immediate use."

She cited a continued influx of interest from buyers in California, Washington and New York. "Florida has welcomed wealth," she said. "Anybody that can afford to be in Palm Beach wants to be."

  • Additional reporting by Katherine Clarke

data.title: How I Used AI to Make My Grandson a Children's Book for Less Than $200 — WSJ
data.description:
By Ken Wells

Parents and grandparents who make up stories for their children and grandchildren often think: "I would love to turn this into an illustrated book."

And then they check into costs and learn that illustrating a 32-page book by a top-notch artist can run up to $20,000 — and that doesn't include printing.

If you have that kind of money, or if you think your book has commercial potential, by all means hire an illustrator. But now there is another way for hobbyists: Artificial-intelligence programs, among them Adobe's Firefly, Neolemon, OpenArt and ChatGPT, that are all capable of creating first-rate, suitable-for-printing images.

I know firsthand that illustrators are expensive, because two years ago I paid an artist $3,600 to draw a dozen illustrations for a self-published children's Christmas book inspired by, and featuring likenesses of, my first two grandchildren. For my next children's book, a surprise birthday present for my third grandchild, Sawyer, I decided to test AI instead.

Sawyer turns one in December, so anything I produced would have to be colorful, bright and short to keep his attention. And it would be full of illustrations that looked like him and his parents.

I came up with a fantastical story involving a loon and a lone boy, and gave it the title "Little Sawyer's Giant Adventures," with this beginning:

Sawyer would come each year with his parents to his grandparents' cabin on a pond in Maine.

He was little, but he dreamed big.

He dreamed of a giant moose named Marvin.

He dreamed of a giant beaver named Bucky.

He dreamed of a giant loon named Louie.

The program I used, Firefly, is included in my $70-a-month Adobe software subscription. For that, I get 6,000 credits a month toward creating high-resolution illustrations, at 300 credits per image.

Like Adobe, most of these programs let you experiment with creating lo-res images free, but you'll need a subscription to do the kind of heavy lifting involved in my project, generating 23 hi-resolution illustrations. For ordinary consumers, subscriptions run from as little as $10 a month to the $70 a month I pay. If you run out of credits, providers are thrilled to sell you more.

Firefly and other AI models operate on plain word prompts typed into a dialogue box. You also must choose the size of the illustration and its resolution — in other words, how crisp and detailed it looks. I burned up 3,600 credits — and had to start over — before I settled on the specs that worked best. So, that is lesson No. 1: Plan ahead.

To create the images, I uploaded pictures of that I wanted Firefly to use as references for the illustrations: one of our log cabin; a headshot of Sawyer; and a picture of his parents. Firefly — well, most of the time — will put those reference pictures in the image at the place of your choosing and dress them to your liking.

I instructed Firefly to give me an image for an "illustrated children's book" using the cabin and the pond as the backdrops. Further, I typed, "Have the boy standing on the pond bank while his parents are watching from the cabin porch. Dress them all in summery hiking clothes." Firefly blew me away on two tries by coming up with this:

It was the look, feel and personalization I wanted. Of course, it wasn't literal (or perfect). Firefly aged Sawyer into a toddler. The pond could be mistaken for a river. And, in the picture, his parents are the same height when, in fact, his mom is taller — something quite clear in the reference image I'd sent. I asked Firefly to fix it, but on three tries the image came back unchanged. Nine hundred credits wasted; cue the annoyance.

Telling Firefly to keep the style it had created, I asked it to put the boy in successive scenes in which he is dreaming of a giant moose, then a giant beaver, then a giant loon. They came back as instructed, but with no variation: Sawyer is in the same sleeping position in the same room, decor unchanged, in each frame.

I had also erred. There was nothing in the dream bubbles to show that the critters were giants. Since Louie the Loon was the vehicle for Sawyer's adventure, I asked Firefly to keep the image it had produced but put the loon next to a tiny red speedboat for perspective. And, oh, add a stuffed giraffe and loon to Sawyer's bedside to add variety to the decor. Bingo: It produced this image:

I then had Firefly remake the giant moose and giant beaver images similarly. Lesson No. 2: Be specific in what you want. (And now you can see how easy it is to burn through credits.)

After dreaming of Louie, Sawyer is out paddling with his parents in a kayak when they see an ordinary-looking loon. Sawyer knows it is the Louie of his dreams and tells his parents so as he waves to the loon and calls out his name. And, of course, the loon is Louie, who is lonesome and has a secret: At night, he becomes a giant who avoids other loons because he fears they will be jealous of his transformation. He's glad Sawyer waved to him and shows up at the cabin dock that night for a visit.

Using the dream scene above as the reference image, I asked Firefly to create an image of Sawyer coming out to meet Louie on the dock. The first try was good — except that Sawyer comes out wearing a life vest. I asked Firefly to keep the image but delete the life jacket. Perfect:

Sawyer convinces the loon to take him on a flying journey. I asked Firefly to show Louie offering Sawyer — wearing a "flying hat" and a life vest for good measure — his wing. My prompt was long and complicated, but Firefly delivered:

At my prompting, Firefly then created a beautiful image of Sawyer and Louie taking off, which I placed on the page under large text reading: "A giant loon can go wherever it wants to go." That was a setup for a series of silly images in which they visit, among others, the Man in the Moon, and see "astronauts trying to eat spaghetti." I laughed out loud when Firefly produced this in about two minutes:

Firefly was also able to create an alluring cover and back cover — something that saved me a few hundred dollars if I'd hired a professional (although I did have to purchase 2,000 extra credits for an additional $11.49 to complete that). The self-publishing site I used, BookBaby, charged $99 to print the 32-page book and ship me a proof copy.

The process requires patience and planning, and there is a learning curve that might be intimidating to the techno-challenged. And the glitches I described weren't the only ones. More than once, Firefly mysteriously injected text or captions into images. For a scene involving Sawyer in the kayak with his parents, Firefly put the kayak on the pond bank.

Still, all in all I was thrilled with the results — and am on to my next project.

Write to reports@wsj.com. You can read a PDF of "Little Sawyer's Giant Adventures" with all of the illustrations on Ken Wells's website at bayoubro.com.

HOLIDAY GIFT GUIDE

data.title: Travel Woes Persist as Airlines Race to Reset After Groundstop — WSJ
data.description:
By Joseph Pisani

The groundstop is over but the pain at the airport isn't.

Nearly 3,900 flights were canceled and more than 2,300 were delayed on Saturday, a day after the Federal Aviation Administration grounded flights nationwide for four hours because of technical issues.

"Operations are slowly returning to normal," Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Saturday in a social-media post. "You will continue to see some delays and cancellations as carriers reschedule flights and reposition aircraft/crews where they are needed most."

Friday's schedule disruptions left planes and crew members out of place for their next flights, and undoing the chaos caused by the groundstop is expected to take days.

At New York's John F. Kennedy International Airport on Saturday, flights were canceled minutes before boarding was supposed to start, with announcers citing staffing issues. Airlines, including United, Delta and American, said they would waive ticket-change fees. Airports encouraged people to check their flight status to avoid long wait times.

Duffy blamed the groundstop on old technology, and he used a press conference at the White House on Friday to plead with Congress to approve funding to upgrade the country's air-traffic system, an overhaul he said would cost $50 billion. Without it, he said outages could happen again.

"We have old switches, old routers. We use 1980s little copper lines," he said at that news conference. "It's an old system that went down."

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters that there wasn't any indication that the outage resulted from a cyberattack, but didn't rule it out.

Mullin attributed the outage to "putting patches into the system" and said that new equipment and technology overwhelmed the older system.

After the groundstop lifted about 8:15 p.m. ET on Friday, a group of travelers inside Terminal C at New York's LaGuardia Airport thought they were lucky: Their flight to Minneapolis was the last in the terminal that hadn't been canceled, and a gate agent said the plane and crew were ready to go.

Then, a new gate agent approached with the bad news: Like so many others, Flight 2349 had been canceled, too.

Write to Joseph Pisani at joseph.pisani@wsj.com

data.title: "Never thought I would come this far": Harmanpreet Kaur on wax statue alongside Sachin Tendulkar, MS Dhoni
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- Indian women's cricket team star Harmanpreet Kaur on Saturday said she never imagined that her journey in cricket would bring her the recognition of having a wax statue alongside legends Sachin Tendulkar and MS Dhoni, describing the honour as a great achievement and appreciation of years of hard work and struggle.

Harmanpreet's wax statue was unveiled in Jaipur on Friday and will be placed alongside those of former India cricketers Sachin Tendulkar and MS Dhoni.

Answering an ANI query during a media interaction at an Omaxe Ltd. event in Dwarka, Harmanpreet said she had grown up watching Tendulkar and Dhoni play on television and never thought she would one day be featured alongside them through a wax statue.

"To be honest, when I started playing cricket, I never thought I would come this far. I think it is a great achievement for me. I have always watched Sachin Tendulkar, MS Dhoni and others playing on television. I also got an opportunity to meet them personally, but I never imagined that one day a wax statue and all these things would also come my way," she said.

Reflecting on her journey, the Indian cricketer said she has always remained focused on improving her game and contributing to the country, adding that recognition and achievements along the way were beyond what she had initially imagined.

"I believe it is all about continuing to work hard. You never know what all things life has in store for you. I have always focused on what I want to achieve in cricket, how I can improve my game and how I can take the country forward," she said.

The 2025 ODI World Cup-winning skipper also expressed happiness over the appreciation she has received for her years of hard work and struggles, saying she hoped her journey would encourage young girls to dream big.

"I think these things will keep coming, and I am really happy that all the hard work and struggles I have faced over the years are being appreciated today. I hope that seeing all these things will motivate young girls as well and encourage them to dream big. So, yeah, I am very, very happy about that," she added.

Omaxe Ltd. Managing Director Mohit Goel said Harmanpreet Kaur's journey reflects determination and leadership, adding that the event aimed to celebrate women's achievements and encourage young sporting talent. He also highlighted the company's vision of bringing sports, commerce, entertainment and social experiences together at The Omaxe State.

"Harmanpreet Kaur's journey is an example of determination, leadership and breaking barriers. Hosting her at The Omaxe State gave us an opportunity to celebrate women's achievements while encouraging young sporting talent. We believe sports can play an important role in bringing communities together and inspiring future generations. At The Omaxe State, our vision is to create a destination where sports, commerce, entertainment and social experiences coexist, offering people more opportunities to connect and engage," he said.

Earlier, in March this year, Omaxe also unveiled India's first dedicated 'Pink Stand', named after Harmanpreet Kaur, at its upcoming 30,000-seat cricket stadium in Dwarka.

The initiative is aimed at enhancing safety and comfort for women spectators, marking a significant step towards inclusivity in sports infrastructure in the country.

data.title: Coal India arm Mahanadi Coalfields IPO to hit Dalal Street on November 19
data.description:
Mahanadi Coalfields, a subsidiary of the country's largest coal mining company, Coal India, will open its initial public offering (IPO) for public subscription on November 19. This will be the second mainboard IPO to open next week, alongside that of Crystal Crop Protection.

The IPO comprises an offer for sale (OFS) of 66.18 crore equity shares by promoter Coal India, representing 10 percent of Mahanadi Coalfields' total paid-up equity capital.

As a result, the entire proceeds from the offer, excluding issue expenses, will go to the selling shareholder, Coal India, and the company will not receive any funds from the IPO.

Moneycontrol was the first to report that Mahanadi Coalfields was likely to launch its maiden public offering next week, with the issue size expected to be around $1 billion, or approximately Rs 9,500 crore.

IPO Schedule

The one-day anchor book will open on November 18 for institutional investors, while the IPO will close for public subscription on November 23.

The share allotment is likely to be finalised on November 25, and Mahanadi Coalfields shares are scheduled to list on the stock exchanges on November 27.

Mahanadi Coalfields will be the third Coal India subsidiary to get listed on the stock exchanges, after Bharat Coking Coal and Central Mine Planning & Design Institute.

The country's largest coal-producing company has reserved 3.3 crore equity shares, or 5 percent of the offer size, for its employees and 6.61 crore shares, or 10 percent of the total offer, for Coal India shareholders.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

Of the net offer, excluding the portions reserved for employees and shareholders, 50 percent has been earmarked for qualified institutional buyers (QIBs), 15 percent for non-institutional investors (NIIs), and the remaining 35 percent for retail investors.

Business

Mahanadi Coalfields was incorporated in April 1992 after being carved out of South Eastern Coalfields to meet the country's growing energy requirements by increasing coal production from two coalfields — Talcher and Ib Valley — in Odisha. These coalfields have estimated coal resources of approximately 106.76 billion tonnes.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

It is the largest coal producer among Coal India's subsidiaries, accounting for 28.4 percent of Coal India's total coal production in FY26 and 21 percent of domestic coal production. Its resources predominantly comprise thermal-grade non-coking coal.

Financial Performance

Mahanadi Coalfields reported a 6.7 percent year-on-year increase in profit to Rs 4,880.7 crore for the six months ended September 2026. Revenue rose 9.3 percent to Rs 16,093 crore during the same period compared with the corresponding period of the previous fiscal year.

For the financial year ended March 2026, however, profit declined 1.2 percent to Rs 10,698.1 crore, while revenue fell 2.6 percent to Rs 30,549.6 crore compared with the previous year.

SBI Capital Markets, Axis Capital, BOB Capital Markets, IDBI Capital Markets & Securities, and IIFL Capital Services have been appointed as merchant bankers to the Mahanadi Coalfields IPO.

data.title: Fed's Collins says gradual rate hikes best to manage economic risks
data.description:
Key points:
  • Fed's Collins says steady, gradual rate rises best manages economic risks
  • Collins says she expects Fed to go farther with rate hikes given data from recent months
  • Collins says financial conditions may provide some economic restraint

By Michael S. Derby

Federal Reserve Bank of Boston President Susan Collins said on Saturday she supported a steady pace of modest interest rate increases because that path of action better managed economic uncertainties.

When it comes to moving monetary policy to a tighter footing, "a steady, gradual path seems appropriate to me at the moment. But I'm open-minded," Collins told reporters at a conference held by her bank on housing issues in Boston.

“I do see the risks as two-sided on the real side of the economy," Collins said, with inflation high and its gains broadening throughout the economy, while the job market was stable with the potential to accelerate.

At the same time, there are the ongoing risks of more shocks hitting the economy, Collins said. Furthermore, “it's possible that the rise in medium to longer term rates that we've seen since the beginning of the year may actually weigh on demand more than I'm thinking,” and serve as another source of restraint on economic activity, she said.

For now, all of that argues against the Fed shifting to a more aggressive pace of rate rises to contain inflation that has overshot the Fed’s 2% target for more than five years, Collins said.

RATE INCREASES IN DECEMBER, JANUARY SEEN

The Fed last raised rates in September, and it is widely expected to lift its current 3.75% to 4% interest rate target range by a quarter percentage point at the December 8-9 monetary policy meeting, following that with another increase in January.

Most Fed officials have signaled support for steady and small increases to help lower inflation, but last week's price data and the comments of Fed Governor Christopher Waller have suggested some on the Fed may want a bigger increase next month.

A number of Fed officials have said a more measured pace of rate increases allows the economy time to adjust to the rise in borrowing costs.

Collins cautioned that her expectation that the Fed can move gradually "doesn't necessarily mean a particular cadence." She also reiterated that the data flow from recent months has shifted where the Fed could end up in its current tightening cycle.

“I do think that the price data we've seen over the past three months — and the labor market on a stronger footing — does make me think that the path of policy rates over the, you know, next year might be a bit higher than I had thought a couple of months ago,” Collins said.

data.title: Tata Sons listing row: Why Tata Trusts vice-chairmen are defending their RBI outreach
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- Tata Trusts vice-chairmen Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh have defended the group's engagement with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) over the proposed stock market listing of Tata Sons, saying that an adverse regulatory decision should not be viewed as a failure of advocacy.

In a joint letter responding to senior advocate Darius Khambata, the two said the engagement with the central bank had been a sustained process involving discussions and several steps taken by the company, reported Business Standard.

"The record does not support that description," the letter from Srinivasan and Singh to Tata Trusts said.

The response follows Khambata's recent criticism of the developments at Tata Sons' board meeting on September 17, which he described as a "day of infamy" for the Tata group. Khambata, who stepped down as a trustee of Tata Trusts earlier this week, had also questioned the effectiveness of Tata Sons' engagement with the RBI on the listing issue.

Srinivasan and Singh said the engagement with the RBI began in 2023 and subsequently resulted in Tata Sons repaying its outstanding debt and submitting an application for deregistration in March 2024.

"The trustees were kept informed throughout, and neither you nor any other trustee described the effort as inadequate at the time." They added that if Khambata referred to meaningful engagement as advocacy that secures preferential treatment or circumvents the applicable rules, "then that would not be consistent with the Tata model you seek to uphold".

They maintained that discussions with the regulator continued beyond the initial engagement and that the outcome should not be interpreted as a failure of the company's efforts.

The two vice-chairmen have differing positions from the Tata Trusts leadership on the listing issue. Srinivasan is currently a nominee director on the Tata Sons board, alongside Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata. Singh also served as a nominee director on the board until September 2025.

Both Srinivasan and Singh have supported the listing of Tata Sons, while Tata Trusts adopted a resolution in July 2025 favouring keeping the holding company privately held.

The dispute centres on the RBI's September 2022 decision to classify Tata Sons as an upper-layer non-banking financial company (NBFC). Under the regulatory framework, upper-layer NBFCs are required to list their shares within three years.

On Khambata calling listing an existential threat to Tata Trusts in his November 2 letter, the latest communication from Srinivasan and Singh, said: "We have seen no evidence for that proposition. Novo Nordisk, Hershey, Lundbeck and Demant are each controlled or anchored by a foundation or trust, and each is listed. Closer to home, Tata Consultancy Services is listed and controlled by Tata Sons, and its standing as a Tata institution has never been questioned. In our view, an institution's character is preserved by the quality of its governance and accountability, not by its listing status."

Seeking to avoid the listing requirement, Tata Sons repaid its outstanding borrowings and applied to the RBI in March 2024 for deregistration as a core investment company (CIC).

The company sought to establish that it no longer met the criteria requiring it to remain registered as an NBFC, which would potentially allow it to remain privately held.

However, in September 2026, the RBI rejected Tata Sons' deregistration application, effectively bringing the mandatory listing requirement back into focus.

Noel Tata has opposed the proposed listing and suggested restructuring the holding company as an alternative.

Defending the case for listing, Srinivasan and Singh cited the experience of several Tata group companies and their substantial investments to argue that greater transparency would not necessarily restrict long-term business ambitions.

They said disclosure requirements and accountability mechanisms could strengthen capital allocation and corporate governance rather than constrain strategic decision-making.

"Disclosure and accountability bring discipline to how capital is allocated; they do not limit vision," the two said in their letter.

On Khambata's concern that listing would decouple Tata Sons from Tata Trusts and adversely impact the model on which the group rests, the two trustees' letter said: "We do not agree. The Trusts would remain shareholders of Tata Sons before and after listing, and their shareholding, dividends and the philanthropy those dividends fund would be unaffected." The exchange highlights the continuing differences within the Tata leadership over the future ownership and regulatory status of Tata Sons, the holding company of the $100-billion-plus Tata group. The RBI's decision has added urgency to the debate over whether the company should pursue a stock market listing or explore restructuring options to retain its private status.

data.title: Tesla Opens Sales Of Autonomous Cybercab for 'Select' Customers — WSJ
data.description:
By Sean O'Kane

Tesla has begun taking orders for personally owned versions of its Cybercab, which has no steering wheel or pedals.

The company said in posts on X on Friday that "select customers are now being invited to purchase Cybercab for personal use" at an estimated purchase price of $29,990. The vehicle requires a $299-per-month subscription to Tesla's autonomy software and a $1,000 nonrefundable deposit.

The autonomous, two-door vehicle was previously only deployed in Tesla's taxi fleet.

The vehicles are estimated to be delivered in December, according to Tesla's posts.

The announcement comes after Tesla and its Chief Executive Elon Musk spent years promising the company would sell fully autonomous vehicles to regular customers. In 2016, Tesla claimed that all vehicles it was making at the time had the hardware necessary to become fully self-driving. In 2019, Musk predicted Tesla would have "over a million robotaxis" on the roads by the following year.

Those promises have yet to materialize, but Tesla has recently made progress toward its autonomous goals. The company has operated "Robotaxi" versions of its Model Y SUV in Austin, Texas since June 2025. That self-driving ride-hailing service has since expanded to other cities in Texas and Florida.

In September, Tesla started adding Cybercabs to the Austin fleet. The gold, two-seater vehicle has no manual driving controls that are required by federal motor vehicle safety standards.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has opened an investigation into whether the Cybercab complies with these regulations. Tesla has told the safety regulator that it believes the Cybercab meets the standards, but the company hasn't publicly explained its position.

Tesla and NHTSA didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

The late Friday announcement also signals a possible shift for Tesla's autonomous strategy. On a call with investors in October, Musk said "the vast majority of the Cybercab stuff will be essentially Tesla-owned."

In the social-media posts Friday, the company explained in fine print that the personally owned Cybercabs will only be available to operate "in supported service areas." Ashok Elluswamy, Tesla's head of AI, said in a post that the vehicles will "work unsupervised inside all the same geo locations as" the company's existing Robotaxi service.

Tesla's claim that the Cybercab can only be purchased for personal use means buyers won't be able to immediately make money with the vehicle. The company had previously solicited interest in September for "Cybercab fleet vehicle purchasing." Musk has pitched shareholders on the idea that small fleet owners could manage Cybercabs "like a shepherd tends their flock."

Musk has also promised that customers would be able to add their own Teslas to a larger, autonomous ride-hailing network. On Tesla's October call with investors, Elluswamy said this functionality would come in the second quarter of 2027.

Write to Sean O'Kane at sean.okane@wsj.com

data.title: Why the Microsoft Outage Came at the Worst Possible Time for the Stock — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Callum Keown and Kit Norton

Microsoft has had a rough few days, not quite Nvidia levels of bad, but far from ideal.

A global outage hit the company's Outlook, Teams, and Copilot AI assistant, impacting users across more than 70 countries, according to outage tracker Downdetector. More than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 services, as well as governments and organizations around the world.

As of Saturday morning, the number of users reporting issues with Microsoft products to Downdetector had dwindled, and Microsoft's service health status webpage was showing that consumer products were operational.

A Microsoft account on X dedicated to posting updates on Microsoft 365 status issues wrote early Saturday morning that the company "completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions."

The timing of the outage is particularly inconvenient for Microsoft. Anthropic launched a new suite of office tools on Tuesday and the market saw it as a direct challenge to the tech giant.

Engineers worked to fix the problem for more than a day. At 11:40 a.m. Eastern time Friday, the company again apologized for the disruption and said it was seeing "broad recovery and stability" across its services.

"Given the scale of demand, we restored services gradually, validating stability at each stage. While this took longer, it helped ensure a stable restoration," Microsoft said.

The company's updates illustrate it was a slog of an effort to restore services. Microsoft said in a status update shortly after 10 p.m. Thursday, more than nine hours after first confirming it was investigating the issue, that changes "applied to improve serviceability" weren't "taking as expected."

Over the intervening hours, however, Microsoft reported improvements in service availability, with email queues significantly reduced and approaching normal levels.

The company has also said the outage was a technical issue and wasn't related to cybersecurity or artificial-intelligence agents. Microsoft will provide a full post-incident report once the company's review is complete.

The stock rose 0.2% to $523.88 on Friday, recovering from a drop of more than 2% in the premarket session.

It's been a tough week for the tech giant. Reports of OpenAI's latest figures suggested that it's some way behind Anthropic in the AI race.

That's bad news for Microsoft, which has a 24% stake in the OpenAI and a much smaller investment in Anthropic.

Investors, however, might be in for some good news next week when the tech company holds its "Ignite" conference. Microsoft is expected to focus on advancements around its cloud platform, Azure, and Copilot.

"We expect the event to reinforce confidence in Microsoft's AI growth narrative," Citi analyst Tyler Radke said in a research note.

Write to Callum Keown at callum.keown@dowjones.com and Kit Norton at kit.norton@barrons.com

data.title: Italy Fines Meta €805 Mln Over Android Gallery Data Access
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Italy's privacy regulator has imposed a 805 million euros penalty on Meta Platforms Ireland after finding that the company accessed photos, videos, and related information stored on Android devices without obtaining specific user permission.

The case focuses on a Facebook feature that offered users photo and video suggestions from their phone galleries while they were browsing the app. According to the authority, the feature allowed access to gallery content without providing users with clear information and a separate consent process.

The regulator's investigation began after a consumer complaint and included a technical review of how the feature operated. Following its findings, the authority ordered Meta to switch off the feature by default within 60 days and seek explicit consent before accessing gallery content.

The decision adds to growing scrutiny of how major technology companies handle personal data and user permissions in mobile applications

data.description:
The technology sector grabbed spotlight this week after Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO amid reports of extramarital affairs, while a major Microsoft outage disrupted business and government operations across Asia and the U.S.

The tech-focused Nasdaq Composite Index closed in the red on Friday. The top S&P 500 technology gainers and losers for the last week are as follows:

Top Gainers:

  • AMD +18.93%
  • Broadcom +18.16%
  • Monolithic Power Systems +16.81%
  • Arista Networks +15.57%
  • Ciena +15.29%

Top Losers:

  • First Solar -14.79%
  • Nvidia -12.75%
  • Super Micro Computer -6.59%
  • Global Payments -5.68%

Here are some of the important technology stories from this week:

Nvidia CEO Huang resigns

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned on Thursday, the company said, adding that he will be replaced on an interim basis by CFO Colette Kress.

Wall Street brokerages downgraded the stock, with GF Securities became the latest investment firm to lower rating amid concerns about its future.

“As said, the uncertainty is likely to linger and turned out to be a real announcement by Nvidia, considering Jensen’s leadership is crucial to Nvidia (as well as the AI industry).” GF analyst Jeff Pu wrote.

The stock also received downgrades from William Blair, Melius Research, Evercore and KeyBanc, signalling raised concerns about the company's leadership and succession plans. Nvidia stock closed 2% lower on Friday.

Microsoft outage affects Outlook, Teams

Microsoft’s widespread outage affecting services such as Outlook and Teams persisted for hours, disrupting users, businesses, and some government operations across Asia and the U.S. as the company worked to resolve the issue.

The company said it was trying different ways to identify the cause of the problem and get its servers back online. However, it did not have any indication that the outage was caused by malicious activity.

Shares of Microsoft closed in the green on Friday after it said it continues to make 'sustained improvements' in restoring outage.

Cisco in focus after Q1 results

Cisco’s stronger-than-expected earnings and outlook were overshadowed by pressure on hardware margins. The company’s Q1 results featured 43% year-over-year growth in its Networking business segment.

However, analysts were quite positive despite the stock trading lower on Friday.

"The Company is benefitting from a Networking super-cycle that continues to have legs and is driven by five key trends: AI wins with Hyperscalers, Campus refresh and modernization, security-driven upgrades for the AI era, sovereign infrastructure, and hybrid data centers for Enterprises," said BofA analyst Tal Liani.

Other tech headlines include Applied Materials reporting fiscal fourth-quarter results and guidance that topped Wall Street's forecast. Analysts say the results pointed to strong semiconductor equipment demand, AI-related spending, and improving visibility into future factory projects.

CoreWeave is planning to raise at least $4B through an investment-grade loan, with Morgan Stanley and Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group leading the potential financing, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

data.title: Notable analyst calls this week: Nvidia, Broadcom and AMD among top picks
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SP500) closed in the red on Friday, as investors assessed the uncertainty in the broader AI space following the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang amid reports of extramarital affairs.

Wall Street had a slew of upgrades and downgrades from analysts. Here are some of the major calls for the week:

Nvidia hit with downgrades after Jensen Huang ouster

Nvidia saw a wave of downgrades and price-target cuts this week as analysts warned that the leadership uncertainty could weigh on the stock.

William Blair downgraded Nvidia to Market Perform, saying Huang's likely departure and heightened scrutiny of the company would be a "significant overhang on Nvidia shares in the near term." Evercore downgraded Nvidia to In Line and cut its price target to $186, from $330, citing the prospect of further valuation multiple compression.

Meanwhile, Melius Research cut the stock to Hold, saying it was difficult to assess the situation, comparing it with Hewlett-Packard's leadership crisis in 2010. KeyBanc also downgraded the company to Sector Weight from Overweight, citing increased strategic, organizational, and execution risks.

RBC lowered its PT to $230 from $330 but maintained its Outperform rating, saying a potential change at the top and congressional hearings could create an overhang. Oppenheimer cut it to Market Perform.

“As said, the uncertainty is likely to linger and turned out to be a real announcement by Nvidia, considering Jensen’s leadership is crucial to Nvidia (as well as the AI industry).” GF Securities analyst Jeff Pu wrote and lowered his rating on Nvidia to Hold from Buy, while cutting his price target to $188 from $235.

Earlier in the week, Morgan Stanley removed its top pick label on Nvidia.

Broadcom in focus after Rothschild downgrade

Rothschild & Co. downgraded Broadcom to Neutral, while adding there is potential upside to be had for investors.

“Guidance implies Broadcom trades at 11x FY28 EPS,” said Rothschild analyst Mike Harrison. “But this counts for little when both the quality and the durability of earnings are under scrutiny.

Harrison also lowered his price target on Broadcom to $398 from $595.

“Broadcom’s alignment with Anthropic and OpenAI means the frontier labs need to establish sustained primacy over open models and become self-financing in short order. Beyond this, the market needs reassurance that Google’s customer-owned tooling efforts will not become widespread. The upside potential to Broadcom shares from clearing these hurdles is appreciable but is unlikely to occur quickly,” he added.

AMD upgraded on potential benefit from Nvidia falloutWilliam Blair upgraded AMD to Outperform from Market Perform, citing an opportunity to benefit from the Nvidia related fallout.

“We see a runway for shares to work from here, with Instinct share gains offering additional upside as AMD stays focused on execution while its largest competitor, Nvidia, contends with a growing leadership and regulatory imbroglio,” William Blair analyst Sebastien Naji said.

Naji also pointed out that the Dr. Lisa Su-led AMD is “in the early innings of a multiyear earnings growth trajectory as it continues to execute in server CPUs.”

Palo Alto upgraded ahead of Q1 results

Palo Alto Networks was upgraded to Overweight by KeyBanc Capital Markets ahead of the cybersecurity firm reporting fiscal first-quarter results on Nov. 18.

"We are upgrading shares of PANW to Overweight as we expect security budgets to accelerate through 2027, Palo a leading beneficiary of the trend toward consolidation with strong product offerings in key areas to secure AI and defend against the accelerated AI threat environment, and Palo out-executing many of its cyber peers," analyst Eric Heath wrote and put a $380 price target on Palo Alto shares.

Roblox downgraded to Neutral by Citi

Citi downgraded Roblox to Neutral from Buy, citing concerns over slowing engagement and potential risks to bookings growth. The brokerage maintained its $55 price target.

Citi analyst Jason Bazinet flagged four areas of concern, including waning popularity of Steal An Egg, a lack of emerging hit experiences, potential competition from Grand Theft Auto VI, and uncertainty around booking growth.

Loop Capital upgraded Autodesk to Buy from Hold, citing improving growth expectations.

Baird upgraded Domino's Pizza to Outperform from its previous rating, citing a clearer path to improved same-store sales and franchisee profitability. The brokerage also raised its price target to $400 from $320.

The fresh lease covers the building’s third, fourth, fifth and sixth floors, with a chargeable area of 2,62,350 sq ft and a carpet area of 1,94,140 sq ft. The company will pay a monthly rent of ₹1.79 crore, translating into a rental rate of ₹68 per sq ft.

The lease commenced on November 1, 2025, while the registration took place on November 2, 2026. Swiggy has paid a security deposit of ₹10.75 crore for the property.

The rental agreement includes an escalation clause of 15 per cent every three years over the 10-year tenure, which will increase the company’s rental commitments over the lease period.

The property is owned by Sumadhura Capitol Towers Private Ltd, which is the landlord for the transaction.

The lease adds to the office space commitments of the food and grocery delivery company in Bengaluru, where it is headquartered.

data.title: Mercedes-Benz Freezes New Investment In Germany, Puts Factory Closures On The Table As Cost Crisis Deepens
data.description:
With China sales falling 31% in Q3 2026 and its full-year passenger car margin forecast cut to 2-3%, Mercedes-Benz is facing a difficult question - how much of its manufacturing future can Germany still afford?

Mercedes-Benz is no longer treating factory closures in Germany as a distant restructuring possibility. The luxury carmaker has now put the option firmly on the table, freezing all further investments at its German sites as management struggles to bring down manufacturing costs and restore profitability.

In a significant escalation of its confrontation with employee representatives, Mercedes-Benz Chief Production Officer Michael Schiebe confirmed that the company's management board had jointly decided to halt further investments in German locations. The decision was communicated to employees through an internal company interview published on November 12, 2026, according to Reuters.

The message from management was unusually blunt. Britta Seeger, a member of the company's board of management, acknowledged that Mercedes-Benz was now being forced to examine in detail which German facilities it could financially sustain. While management maintains that it wants to avoid factory closures, Seeger conceded that the possibility must now be examined more seriously.

This is a considerable escalation for a company whose identity and industrial history are deeply tied to Germany. It also exposes the uncomfortable reality facing the country's automotive industry, a globally recognised manufacturing reputation is no longer enough to compensate for an increasingly expensive domestic production base.

And Mercedes-Benz's decision is not simply about cutting costs. It reflects a business under pressure from multiple directions, including falling sales in China, intensifying competition, weaker profitability and an increasingly difficult transition towards electric mobility.

China Has Become A Serious Problem For Mercedes-Benz

One of the biggest reasons behind the deteriorating financial picture is China, a market that Mercedes-Benz once relied on heavily to drive sales and profitability.

For years, China was a crucial market for German luxury manufacturers. However, the competitive landscape has changed dramatically. Domestic manufacturers have become increasingly sophisticated, offering feature-rich vehicles, advanced software and competitive pricing. International luxury brands are finding it harder to command the premium they once enjoyed.

Mercedes-Benz's own sales figures underline the problem. The company sold 5,51,900 passenger cars in China in 2025, a decline of 19 per cent compared with the previous year. The situation deteriorated further in 2026. In the third quarter, Chinese passenger car sales fell 31 per cent year-on-year to 86,800 units. For the first nine months of 2026, sales in China were down 29 per cent to 297,000 units.

This is not a minor setback for a company with substantial exposure to the Chinese luxury market. It is a significant deterioration in one of its most important sales regions.

The pressure is also visible in the company's overall passenger car business. Mercedes-Benz Cars delivered 4,07,232 vehicles in Q3 2026, down 7.8 per cent year-on-year. Its revenue declined 5.8 per cent to 22.37 billion euro, while adjusted EBIT fell 50.8 per cent to 560 million euro. The division's adjusted return on sales dropped from 4.8 to 2.5 per cent.

The numbers are particularly concerning because they show that the problem extends beyond sales volumes. Mercedes-Benz is also making considerably less money from the vehicles it sells.

Profitability Has Taken A Hit

The pressure on Mercedes-Benz's finances became even more evident when it revised its 2026 financial guidance on October 28.

The company cut its expected adjusted return on sales for Mercedes-Benz Cars to 2-3 per cent, against its earlier forecast of 3-5 per cent. That is a sharp reduction for a luxury manufacturer that has traditionally relied on premium pricing and healthy margins to support its business.

The wider group is not immune either. Mercedes-Benz reported revenue of 30.7 billion euro in Q3 2026, down 4.5 per cent year-on-year. Adjusted group EBIT declined 15 per cent to 1.78 billion euro. More concerningly, free cash flow from its industrial business fell 87.4 per cent to 172 million euro in the quarter, compared with 1.37 billion euro a year earlier.

For the first nine months of 2026, free cash flow from industrial operations was down 44 per cent to 3.13 billion euro. The company also expects its full-year industrial free cash flow to be significantly below the previous year's level.

The revised outlook is a clear indication that Mercedes-Benz is dealing with more than a temporary slowdown. Its ability to protect margins while funding product development, new technologies and global manufacturing operations is coming under pressure.

US import tariffs have added to the burden. Mercedes-Benz has previously indicated that tariffs cost the company approximately 1 billion euro in profits, further complicating an already difficult operating environment.

German Manufacturing Costs Have Become A Flashpoint

However, the most immediate trigger for the investment freeze is the cost of manufacturing vehicles in Germany. Mercedes-Benz management has argued that the country's production economics are increasingly difficult to justify against alternative manufacturing locations.

According to Schiebe, the cost of an hour of production labour in Germany can be as much as five times higher than at some of the company's facilities in Eastern Europe. That is a substantial cost disadvantage, particularly when manufacturers are competing in price-sensitive segments and facing growing pressure to improve production efficiency.

The comparison with Hungary is especially revealing. Mercedes-Benz's Kecskemét facility has become its largest plant in Europe, while production costs there are reportedly considerably lower than at its German factories. Handelsblatt reported, citing an internal company presentation, that production labour costs at Kecskemét were 75 per cent lower than the average across Mercedes' German plants.

This is precisely the kind of cost difference that makes it difficult for German factories to compete for future production allocations. And Mercedes-Benz is no longer hiding its dissatisfaction with the situation.

The company has been negotiating with its works council and IG Metall, Germany's powerful metalworkers' union, over measures to reduce domestic operating costs. One of management's proposals involves increasing the working week from the collectively agreed 35 hours to 40 hours without additional pay.

The discussions have also involved potential reductions in special employee payments. According to Handelsblatt, Mercedes-Benz is targeting annual savings of around 800 million euro through the proposed measures.

The union has resisted the demands, and negotiations have failed to produce an agreement after months of discussions. The investment freeze is therefore also a pressure tactic. By making future investment conditional on a reduction in labour costs, management is effectively telling employees and their representatives that the existing cost structure cannot continue indefinitely.

But the bigger question is whether the company can resolve its cost problem without damaging the very industrial ecosystem that helped establish its global reputation.

The EV Transition Is Not The Whole Story

Mercedes-Benz's difficulties also need to be viewed against the backdrop of its expensive transition towards electrification.

The company has invested heavily in electric vehicle platforms, battery technology and software while continuing to develop and manufacture internal combustion engine models. Maintaining multiple technology programmes inevitably puts pressure on capital expenditure and production planning.

However, it would be inaccurate to suggest that Mercedes-Benz's electric vehicle business is simply collapsing. Its Q3 2026 results actually showed a 61 per cent increase in battery-electric passenger car sales to 68,428 units. BEV deliveries for the first nine months were up nearly 40 per cent to 1,65,538 units.

The problem is that stronger electric vehicle sales have not been enough to offset the weakness elsewhere in the business, particularly in China. The company is also dealing with lower overall passenger car volumes and substantially weaker adjusted earnings.

In other words, electrification is adding to the complexity of the industry's transformation, but Mercedes-Benz's immediate financial difficulties cannot be blamed on EV adoption alone.

Germany's Automotive Industry Is Facing A Larger Crisis

Mercedes-Benz's decision also raises questions about the future of automotive manufacturing in Germany. The country has long been one of the world's most important automotive manufacturing centres, supported by skilled labour, engineering expertise, established suppliers and globally recognised brands. But those advantages are increasingly being challenged by high operating costs, changing market dynamics and competition from manufacturers with lower-cost production bases.

For Mercedes-Benz, the immediate concern is that the investment freeze could eventually affect the future allocation of new models to German factories. Schiebe has indicated that, without an agreement on cost reductions, new models could instead be produced exclusively outside Germany.

Management has also warned that two factories could face closure if negotiations fail to deliver the required savings. No specific closure decision or final list of affected facilities has been announced.

What This Means For Mercedes-Benz

The immediate investment freeze is a warning to employees, unions and the German automotive industry that Mercedes-Benz is prepared to reconsider the geographical distribution of its manufacturing operations.

The company still has substantial financial resources. Its industrial business reported net liquidity of 31 billion euro at the end of Q3 2026. This is not a company running out of cash. Rather, management is attempting to protect profitability and improve the economics of its manufacturing network before the situation deteriorates further.

But there is an uncomfortable contradiction at the heart of this development. Mercedes-Benz has spent decades building its identity around German engineering and manufacturing. Now, the company is questioning whether manufacturing in its home country makes sufficient commercial sense.

That is a particularly damaging message for Germany's industrial ambitions. If even one of its most recognisable luxury manufacturers is unwilling to commit fresh investment to its domestic factories under the current cost structure, the consequences could extend well beyond Mercedes-Benz.

The company now faces a difficult choice of either securing substantial cost concessions, shift more production abroad or accept that some of its German facilities may no longer have a future.

For a brand that has built much of its global reputation on German engineering, that is a rather stark admission.

Utkarsh Agarwal

BW Reporters

As Editorial Lead of BW Auto World, automotive vertical of BW Businessworld, & Special Correspondent for BW Businessworld, Utkarsh operates at the centre of a rapidly evolving automotive & technology landscape, where the story extends beyond products to business, policy, and shifting consumer behaviour. His work spans product reviews, executive interviews, and feature stories that track and interpret the forces shaping India’s automotive & technology sector. Alongside his core automotive & tech coverage, he also brings prior experience in political, lifestyle, and travel content creation.

data.title: RBI Gives Paytm In-Principle Nod To Revive Wallet Business
data.description:
Six-month deadline for cybersecurity audit and final clearance will determine when the digital payment service can resume

Paytm has received in-principle approval from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to restart its digital wallet business through its subsidiary, Paytm Payments Services Limited (PPSL), potentially reopening a payment service that faced restrictions following regulatory compliance concerns. However, the approval does not permit an immediate relaunch. The company must complete an independent systems and cybersecurity audit and submit the findings to the central bank within six months to secure final clearance.

The development follows regulatory action against Paytm Payments Bank, which was barred from accepting fresh deposits and wallet top-ups in early 2024. The RBI cancelled the bank’s licence in April 2026, further separating the banking entity from the payment services business.

Audit Determines Relaunch Timeline

PPSL must undergo an independent systems audit, including a cybersecurity assessment, before it can resume issuing and operating prepaid payment instruments (PPIs). The audit report must reach the RBI within six months. Failure to meet the deadline will result in the in-principle approval lapsing automatically.

The final approval will determine when the company can restart wallet operations. Until then, the regulatory clearance remains conditional, and the financial impact of a potential relaunch is yet to be established.

Why Paytm Wallet Stopped

Paytm’s wallet service was previously operated through Paytm Payments Bank. In early 2024, the RBI restricted the bank from accepting fresh deposits and allowing wallet top-ups following concerns related to compliance with licensing conditions, know-your-customer (KYC) requirements and governance standards.

The restrictions prevented customers from adding money to their existing wallets, disrupting a key part of the company’s digital payments offering.

Payments Bank And Services

Paytm Payments Bank and Paytm Payments Services are separate entities with different functions. The former operated as a banking entity that held deposits and wallet balances before its licence was cancelled. PPSL, a wholly owned subsidiary of One 97 Communications, handles payment solutions and related business services.

The latest in-principle approval applies to PPSL, not the former banking entity. This distinction is central to any revival of the wallet business, which would operate under the applicable regulatory framework for prepaid payment instruments.

What Customers Can Expect

A relaunch following final approval could allow users to load money into digital wallets, maintain balances and make payments for services such as recharges, ticket bookings and bill payments. The company could also explore additional prepaid payment products, subject to regulatory permissions.

Unlike the Unified Payments Interface (UPI), which transfers funds directly between bank accounts without storing money, a prepaid wallet holds money loaded by the user in advance.

The next stage depends on the audit, regulatory review and final authorisation. Until these requirements are met, customers cannot assume that wallet top-ups and services will resume.
